- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75% of recent high), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above recent peak for next 3–7 days.  
- If sentiment swings sharply from positive to negative, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast by 2–5% in the 2–5 day window following sentiment reversal.  
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.  
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days); apply a 1–2% downward correction for first 5 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “1.00” values, model often overfits; apply a 2–4% downward adjustment to forecast if sentiment remains high for 3+ consecutive days.
